In a quiet brass observatory the first lantern began to glow
A clock beneath the moon kept time for footsteps in the snow
The keeper found a tiny gear behind the cedar door
And heard a distant signal from the lighthouse on the shore
The glass was cold against the palm, a frostbite on the skin
While the needle spun a circle where the winter winds had been
He traced the frost along the pane, a map of where we've been
Before the storm could swallow up the light we used to keep within

A child stepped out from under the eaves, a coat of wool and gray
She held a lantern in her hand, a beacon for the day
